name: Int
measurable_floor
result.type:
∀ {R : Type u_2} [inst : Ring R] [inst_1 : LinearOrder R] [inst_2 : FloorRing R] [inst_3 : TopologicalSpace R]
  [OrderTopology R] [inst_5 : MeasurableSpace R] [OpensMeasurableSpace R], Measurable Int.floor
result.value:
:=
  measurable_to_countable fun x => by simpa only [Int.preimage_floor_singleton] using measurableSet_Ico
result.informal_name: Measurability of the Floor Function from ℝ to ℤ
result.informal_description: The floor function mapping real numbers to integers is measurable with respect to the Borel $\sigma$-algebra on $\mathbb{R}$ and the discrete $\sigma$-algebra on $\mathbb{Z}$.

name: Measurable
floor
result.signature: [OpensMeasurableSpace R] {f : α → R} (hf : Measurable f) : Measurable fun x => ⌊f x⌋
result.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {R : Type u_2} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] [inst_1 : Ring R] [inst_2 : LinearOrder R]
  [inst_3 : FloorRing R] [inst_4 : TopologicalSpace R] [OrderTopology R] [inst_6 : MeasurableSpace R]
  [OpensMeasurableSpace R] {f : α → R}, Measurable f → Measurable fun x => ⌊f x⌋
result.informal_name: Floor of a Measurable Function is Measurable
result.informal_description: If $ f : \alpha \to \mathbb{R} $ is a measurable function with respect to the Borel $ \sigma $-algebra on $ \mathbb{R} $, then the function $ x \mapsto \lfloor f(x) \rfloor $ is also measurable.

result.informal_description: The continuous linear operator $ \mathcal{F} : \mathcal{S}(V, E) \to \mathcal{S}(V, E) $ defined by the Fourier transform, where $ V $ is a finite-dimensional real inner product space and $ E $ is a normed $ \mathbb{C} $-$ \mathbb{K} $-bimodule over a real closed-like field $ \mathbb{K} $. This operator maps Schwartz functions $ f : V \to E $ to their Fourier transforms $ \mathcal{F}f $, preserving the Schwartz space structure through smoothness, polynomial decay, and compatibility with scalar multiplication.

name: Nat
measurable_floor
result.type:
∀ {R : Type u_2} [inst : Semiring R] [inst_1 : LinearOrder R] [inst_2 : FloorSemiring R] [inst_3 : TopologicalSpace R]
  [OrderTopology R] [inst_5 : MeasurableSpace R] [OpensMeasurableSpace R] [IsStrictOrderedRing R], Measurable Nat.floor
result.value:
:=
  measurable_to_countable fun n => by
    rcases eq_or_ne ⌊n⌋₊ 0 with h | h <;> simp [h, Nat.preimage_floor_of_ne_zero, -floor_eq_zero]
result.informal_name: Measurability of the Floor Function in Strict Ordered Rings
result.informal_description: The floor function mapping elements of a strict ordered ring $ R $ to natural numbers $ \mathbb{N} $ is measurable. This means that for every measurable subset $ S \subseteq \mathbb{N} $, the preimage $ \{x \in R \mid \lfloor x \rfloor \in S\} $ is a measurable set in $ R $, where $ R $ is equipped with the Borel $ \sigma $-algebra generated by its order topology and $ \mathbb{N} $ has the discrete $ \sigma $-algebra.
